own_15_g3_promote_gate_upgrade_eligible_: FAIL verdict gives no upward evidence for G3 upgrade. tokenizer_truncation_warning: Truncation rate observed at ~85% (678/800 prompts truncated to fit block_size=512). This is NOT a bug — it's the same recipe as OPT-C and the shim v5 phase2 selftest, all of which use block_size=512. Hellaswag 5-shot context typically exceeds 512 tokens; truncation chops the FRONT of the context (not the continuation). Cross-shim equivalence: both v4 and v5 see the same truncated context (deterministic), so the differential measurement is unaffected. Absolute acc_norm is depressed below CLM v4's likely peak by truncation — but this is consistent across all 4 passes.
honest_c3: C1 — Fresh-init untrained, ALL FOUR passes hover at acc_norm ≈ 0.27-0.28 (random-floor ≈ 0.25 for hellaswag mc-choice). The differential v5_NF=v4_NF=v5_RF=0.27 demonstrates that random-init weights produce essentially identical argmax token rankings regardless of the cross_attn.o_proj scale — when the rest of the network is random, the cross_attn output at any scale is mixed into noise. Only v5_RF moves to 0.28 (+1pp), and even that is well below combined SE 4.48pp. PASS verdict gate (lift_pp_v5>=5pp AND sigdiff) is not met on any axis.

C2 — Substrate differential measured at random-floor confirms the architectural lever (o_proj std 0.02 vs 0.10) does NOT transfer to benchmark accuracy at random-init. This DOES NOT rule out trained-weights transfer (where downstream layers have learned to USE cross_attn signal) — but it removes one of the cheapest empirical paths to demonstrating shim v5 viability. The trained-weights regime requires OPT-B retrain (CLM v4 from scratch with cross_attn.o_proj std=0.10 init scale, $100-300 H100, 1-2 weeks) to test directly. Phase 2 OPT-A verdict §C7 anticipated this caveat.

C3 — Real fixture lift via cross-attn architectural: with shim v5 OPT-A o_proj std=0.10 (5x v4's 0.02), the cross_attn output magnitude is 5x larger entering the residual stream. The fixture train_avg_real.pt has L2≈2.2 (mean_abs≈0.080), so the v5 substrate sees ≈ 5×L2 ≈ 11 units of signal vs ≈ 2.2 for v4 (relative — modulo per-block depth scaling). The empirical lift_pp_v5=+1.0pp tells us this signal magnitude DID reach the logits (else we'd see exact 0pp like v4_RF). But the network's randomness means the signal is mixed into incoherent feature maps — it cannot bias hellaswag preference rankings.

C4 — Stderr at limit=200: bootstrap_iters=1000 produced acc_norm_stderr ≈ 0.0315 for all 4 passes (uniform because acc_norm=0.27-0.28 is in the same neighborhood). Combined stderr for differentials sqrt(2)×0.0315×100 ≈ 4.45pp. The +5pp threshold is BARELY above the noise floor at this limit. A larger limit (n=1000+) would tighten stderr to ~1.4pp and could reveal sub-5pp differentials, but at this BG's $3 budget that scope was out-of-reach. The FAIL verdict is robust at limit=200 because lift_pp_v5=+1pp is well below even a tightened stderr.

C5 — own 15 G3 upgrade eligibility: false. FAIL verdict gives zero upward evidence. Fresh-init evidence ALSO does not prove production-trained-weights substrate viability — the path to G3 upgrade is blocked at both endpoints (fresh-init falsified here; trained-weights collapsed by best.pt overwrite per OPT-C/Phase 2). A complete G3 case now requires architectural change (Path B cross-attn-active SFT loss adjustment, $20-100 H100) OR full re-train (OPT-B, $100-300 H100). Neither falls within this BG's scope.
